problem: Recent Transformer-based VLN methods (DUET and successors) gain performance by adding external knowledge, maps or depth, which inflates model size and FLOPs, and they degrade on long instructions and complex paths. Directly applying Mamba/selective SSMs to VLN performs poorly because SSMs are 1-D and causal, cannot do cross-modal attention, and are weak at input selection.
motivation: Low-cost VLN matters for deployment on real robots. SSMs offer linear complexity and good long-sequence modeling, but the vanilla Mamba drops SR to about 32% on REVERIE (Table 3), so VLN-specific SSM designs are needed.
key_idea: Build a hybrid architecture in which VLN-tailored selective SSMs (Round Selective Scan and the dual-stream Cross-modal Selective State Space Module) first selectively memorize instruction-relevant observations, and Transformer layers then make the action decision.
insight: Mamba layers in a single concatenated stream perform badly (SR 32.25 on REVERIE val unseen), and even Bi-Mamba only reaches 35.61. The dual-stream CS3 gives +3.86 SR over Bi-Mamba (Table 4). The order SSM-then-Transformer is best: SSM+Trans reaches SR 50.81 versus 46.58 for Trans+SSM and 41.92 for SSM+SSM (Table 5). The gain over DUET is larger on long instructions (+7.42 SR for REVERIE instructions over 30 words), which supports the selective memorization claim.
method: Hybrid architecture: selective SSM modules (RSS, CS3) perform selective memorization first, then cross-attention/GASA/self-attention Transformer layers perform action decision-making

Round Selective Scan (RSS): flips the sequence and concatenates it with the original, [x'|flip(x')], scans once so the class token at both ends sees all tokens and compresses the whole sequence in its final state; the two halves of the output are split, the second half is reversed, and they are added

Cross-modal Selective State Space Module (CS3): dual-stream SSM in which B and Δ are built from the source modality y (flipped and concatenated), C is built from the class token of the target modality x, and the final-state output gates x through a residual and norm

Node Encoder: builds the topological map first, encoding the observations of each node with 2 self-attention layers plus average pooling into a compressed node feature (ghost nodes included), while the current node keeps its full view tokens for the local encoder

Global and Local Cross-modal Encoders: global uses GASA, CS3, GASA, cross-attention and GASA over topological nodes; local uses CS3, RSS, cross-attention and self-attention over current-node views; the two action predictions are dynamically fused as in DUET
Lightweight setup: TinyBERT text encoder (hidden 312), state size 16, DUET features and hyperparameters, pretraining with augmented data, and the model ends at 28M parameters and 0.46 GFLOPs

setting.backbone: DUET-style dual-scale graph model with TinyBERT text encoder, ViT features, and SSM modules (RSS, CS3) plus Transformer layers, trained from scratch/finetuned
setting.training_data: R2R/REVERIE training sets plus augmented data (speaker-generated for REVERIE, R2R augmented data) for 100k pretraining steps then 20k finetuning steps; R2R-CE transferred from R2R-pretrained model and finetuned 30 epochs
setting.observation: panoramic RGB (ViT view features); waypoint predictor for R2R-CE
setting.action_space: discrete nav-graph node selection (topological map, ghost nodes, stop); R2R-CE uses waypoint predictor candidates

numbers_note: Table 1 Param/FLOPs for COSMO: 28M and 0.46G. Appendix mentions BEV-feature variant with R2R test SR=71, SPL=62 (text only, not in a table). Ablation tables report SPL 35.93 in Table 4 but 35.83 in Table 5 for the same model.
results: COSMO reaches REVERIE val-unseen SR 50.81 / SPL 35.93 (DUET 46.98 / 33.73) and R2R-CE test SR 47 / SPL 40 (DUET 42 / 36), with only 28M parameters and 0.46 GFLOPs (about 15% of the parameters and 9.3% of the FLOPs of DUET). It is competitive with methods that use extra knowledge or maps, and it beats NaviLLM on REVERIE by 8.66 SR on val unseen.
limitations: Slightly lower SPL than DUET on R2R; the paper attributes this to checkpoint selection by SR+SPL
Still behind the best map/data-scaled methods (e.g. ScaleVLN, BEVBert) in absolute performance
Failure cases remain on ambiguous instructions and on getting close to the target object
